s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of abdominal pain, nausea, and bloody diarrhea with evidence of colonic inflammation
salient_findings: Colonoscopic findings of segmental erythema and ulceration
key_facts: Negative stool cultures and Clostridioides difficile toxin assays
Mild thickening of the mid- and distal descending colon on CT
No evidence of perforation, abscess, or diverticulosis
Segmental erythema and ulceration on colonoscopy
Subepithelial edema, hemorrhage, and acute inflammatory infiltrate on biopsy

raw.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of abdominal pain, nausea, and bloody diarrhea with evidence of colonic inflammation
salient_findings: Colonoscopic findings of segmental erythema and ulceration
key_facts: Negative stool cultures and Clostridioides difficile toxin assays
Mild thickening of the mid- and distal descending colon on CT
No evidence of perforation, abscess, or diverticulosis
Segmental erythema and ulceration on colonoscopy
Subepithelial edema, hemorrhage, and acute inflammatory infiltrate on biopsy

shortlist.label: Ulcerative Colitis
shortlist.why_kept: Segmental erythema and ulceration on colonoscopy, subepithelial edema and acute inflammatory infiltrate on biopsy

shortlist.label: Crohn's Disease
shortlist.why_kept: Mild thickening of the mid- and distal descending colon on CT, elevated C-reactive protein

shortlist.label: Infectious Colitis
shortlist.why_kept: Bloody diarrhea and negative stool cultures and Clostridioides difficile toxin assays

shortlist.label: Microscopic Colitis
shortlist.why_kept: Normal colonoscopy appearance in some segments, subepithelial edema and acute inflammatory infiltrate on biopsy

shortlist.label: Ischemic Colitis
shortlist.why_kept: Mild thickening of the mid- and distal descending colon on CT, absence of granulomas or dysplasia on biopsy

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of worsening crampy abdominal pain, bloody diarrhea, and elevated fecal calprotectin, combined with colonoscopy findings of segmental erythema and ulceration in the descending and sigmoid colon, is consistent with ulcerative colitis. The absence of granulomas on biopsy also supports this diagnosis over Crohn's disease.

rejected.label: Crohn's Disease
rejected.why: Absence of granulomas on biopsy and pattern of colon involvement

rejected.label: Infectious Colitis
rejected.why: Negative stool cultures and Clostridioides difficile toxin assays

rejected.label: Microscopic Colitis
rejected.why: Presence of gross bleeding and ulceration on colonoscopy, which is not typical for microscopic colitis

rejected.label: Ischemic Colitis
rejected.why: No evidence of vascular occlusion or ischemia on CT, and biopsy findings not consistent with ischemic injury
